ox: Incorrect. 0.83 is 1000/1200, the ratio upside down. Specific gravity is the substance's density divided by water's density, with the substance on top.
Correct. SG = ρ(substance) / ρ(water) = 1200 / 1000 = 1.2. Units cancel, so SG has none.
Incorrect. 1200 is the density in kg/m³, not the ratio to water. You still have to divide by 1000.
Incorrect. 1.2 is the right number but the units are wrong. A ratio of two densities has no units, so 'kg/m³' cannot be attached.

p: Specific gravity compares a substance's density to the density of water (1000 kg/m³, or 1 g/cm³). Because it is a ratio of two densities, it has no units. A value above 1 means the substance is denser than water and sinks in it; below 1 it floats.

x4B_001.trap: Reporting 1200, or attaching the units kg/m³; specific gravity is a pure ratio.
x4B_001.eli: Specific gravity is a 'how many times heavier than water' score for the same size of cup.
mem: SG > 1 sinks in water; SG < 1 floats.

fm.f: SG = ρ_substance / ρ_water, where ρ_substance = density of the saline (1200 kg/m³), ρ_water = density of water (1000 kg/m³)
fm.why: We divide by water's density because specific gravity is defined as a ratio against water.

ox: Incorrect. Oxygen content does not change how fast a liquid flows through a tube. The question is about fluid flow, which depends on pressure, radius, length and viscosity.
Incorrect. Radius is unchanged, but viscosity is NOT unchanged. More red cells make blood thicker, so flow changes even though radius stays the same.
Correct. Poiseuille: Q = ΔP·πr⁴ / (8ηL). ΔP, r and L stay the same, but η (viscosity) rises with hematocrit, so Q falls. Thicker blood is harder to push.
Incorrect. Density plays no role in Poiseuille flow. Viscosity (resistance to flow), not density (mass per volume), is what rises with more red cells.

p: Poiseuille's law gives the flow rate of a viscous fluid through a tube: Q = ΔP·πr⁴ / (8ηL). Flow rises with pressure difference and with radius to the FOURTH power, and falls with viscosity and length. Blood viscosity rises with hematocrit, which is why polycythemia makes blood harder to move.

d_4B_12.trap: Thinking more red cells means more flow because more oxygen is carried. Flow rate here is fluid mechanics, not oxygen delivery.
d_4B_12.eli: Blood with more red cells is like switching from water to syrup: it pours more slowly through the same straw.
mem: Flow ∝ r⁴ (a tiny change in radius matters a lot) and ∝ 1/η.
Higher hematocrit → higher viscosity → lower flow.

fm.f: Q = ΔP·π·r⁴ / (8·η·L), where Q = flow rate, ΔP = pressure difference, r = vessel radius, η = viscosity, L = vessel length
fm.v: ΔP, r and L unchanged; η goes UP
fm.s: Q ∝ 1/η, so if η doubles then Q is cut in half
fm.why: We use Poiseuille's law because it tells us how each property of the vessel and the fluid changes flow.

d_4B_12.sc: Change one variable at a time: with pressure and tube fixed, flow moves opposite to viscosity.
d_4B_12.mn: Radius to the Fourth power rules the tube; viscosity is the enemy: thicker = slower.

ox: Correct. Myoglobin has ONE heme and no cooperativity, so its curve is a hyperbola. Its P50 is about 2 mmHg, so it holds O₂ tightly even at very low PO₂ (higher affinity than hemoglobin).
Incorrect. A sigmoidal curve with lower affinity describes HEMOGLOBIN (4 subunits, cooperative, P50 ≈ 26 mmHg), not myoglobin.
Incorrect. Myoglobin does have higher affinity, but a sigmoidal curve requires cooperativity between subunits. Myoglobin has just one, so its curve cannot be sigmoidal.
Incorrect. Hyperbolic is right, but lower affinity is wrong. A P50 of about 2 mmHg is much lower than hemoglobin's 26 mmHg, which means HIGHER affinity.

p: Hemoglobin has four subunits that help each other (cooperativity), giving an S-shaped (sigmoidal) curve with P50 ≈ 26 mmHg. Myoglobin has one subunit, so it simply binds O₂ with a hyperbolic curve and P50 ≈ 2 mmHg. Lower P50 = higher affinity: myoglobin stores O₂ in muscle and releases it only when PO₂ is very low.

d_4B_10.trap: Assuming the sigmoidal curve belongs to the protein with the higher affinity.
d_4B_10.eli: Myoglobin is a warehouse that holds on tight to oxygen; hemoglobin is a delivery truck that drops it off where tissues need it.
mem: Mb: 1 heme, hyperbolic, P50 ≈ 2 mmHg, stores O₂ in muscle.
Hb: 4 hemes, sigmoidal, P50 ≈ 26 mmHg, delivers O₂.
Lower P50 = higher affinity = curve further LEFT.
d_4B_10.sc: Smaller P50 means it grabs O₂ harder, so its curve sits further to the left.
d_4B_10.mn: Mb = Muscle bank (stores O₂). Hb = Hauls and hands off O₂.
